approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would take money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to pay for the government's day-to-day running costs.
The amount would be about five-twelfths of the expected annual funding for these services, not counting new budget measures.
The remaining seven-twelfths and any budget measures would be covered by a separate bill.
It would authorise spending for ordinary annual services of the government.
It would set the appropriation at roughly five-twelfths of the estimated 2019-20 annual amount.
It would exclude 2019-20 Budget measures from this bill.
The government and its departments that receive funding for ordinary annual services.

This bill seeks approval for $4.8 billion in interim appropriations for non‑ordinary annual services, covering five‑twelfths of the estimated 2019‑20 spending, and must be passed before 1 July 2019 to ensure continued program and service delivery.

The coalition proposed supply bills for 2019-20, which Labor will not block. The speaker argued the government cut $715 million from Medicare, $5 billion from education, and gave $80 billion in tax cuts to high-income earners, while debt reached $534.2 billion, and Labor's Fair Go Action Plan includes making multinationals pay fair tax and restoring penalty rates.
